body.objective: Students will be able to name hobbies.
successCriteria: I can name common hobbies in Mandarin
I can say what my hobbies are and what I like doing
I can ask a classmate about their hobbies
body.hook: What do you do after school? Play basketball, draw, listen to music, game with friends? Talking about hobbies is one of the easiest ways to connect with new people in any language. Today you'll learn to share your hobbies in Mandarin.

vocabulary.term: 玩电子游戏 wán diànzǐ yóuxì

study.title: 你的爱好是什么？
study.question: How do I talk about my hobbies in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Sentence patterns:
• 你的爱好是什么？Nǐ de àihào shì shénme? = What is your hobby?
• 我的爱好是画画。Wǒ de àihào shì huà huà. = My hobby is drawing.
• 我喜欢打篮球。Wǒ xǐhuan dǎ lánqiú. = I like playing basketball.
• 我常常听音乐。Wǒ chángcháng tīng yīnyuè. = I often listen to music.
Verbs matter: basketball uses 打 dǎ (hit/play), soccer uses 踢 tī (kick).
Dialogue:
李华 Lǐ Huá：你的爱好是什么？
艾玛 Àimǎ：我的爱好是游泳和看书。你呢？
李华：我喜欢踢足球。我每个周末都踢足球。
艾玛：你也喜欢玩电子游戏吗？
李华：喜欢！我常常跟朋友一起玩。
艾玛：我不太喜欢玩电子游戏，我喜欢画画。
English support: 和 hé = and (joins nouns); 每个周末都 měi gè zhōumò dōu = every weekend; 也 yě = also; 常常 chángcháng = often; 跟朋友一起 gēn péngyou yìqǐ = together with friends; 不太喜欢 bú tài xǐhuan = don't really like.
Activity: Find someone who…: ask classmates "你喜欢…吗？" for six hobbies and collect a name for each "喜欢！"
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Learn hobby vocabulary with the correct verbs
Practise the 我的爱好是 and 我喜欢 patterns
Read the dialogue with a partner
Share your hobbies in three sentences
discussion: How often does Lǐ Huá play soccer?

study.product: Write a short paragraph (5–6 sentences) in characters and pinyin about your hobbies: what they are, how often you do them, who you do them with and one hobby you don't really like.

body.objective: Students will be able to use 会 and 能.
body.iCan: I can use 会 and 能.
successCriteria: I can use 会 for learned skills
I can use 能 and 可以 for ability, possibility and permission
I can talk about what I can and can't do
body.hook: English uses "can" for many things: skills, possibility and permission. Mandarin splits these up: 会 for skills you've learned, 能 for being able to in a situation, and 可以 for permission.

vocabulary.definition: can, be able to (circumstances, physical ability)

study.title: 会, 能, 可以
study.question: How do I say "can" in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Grammar (written for this lesson):
会 huì: skills learned through practice: 我会游泳。(I can swim.) 我会说一点儿中文。(I can speak a little Chinese.) 我不会弹钢琴。(I can't play piano: I never learned.)
能 néng: ability in a situation or physical ability: 我今天不能游泳, 我感冒了。(I can't swim today; I have a cold.) 他能跑十公里。(He is able to run 10 km.)
可以 kěyǐ: permission: 我可以用你的笔吗? (May I use your pen?) 这里不可以拍照。(No photos here.)
Questions: 你会…吗? / 你能…吗? / 我可以…吗?
Skills list: 游泳, 滑冰 huábīng (skate), 滑雪 huáxuě (ski), 做饭 zuò fàn (cook), 画画 huà huà (draw), 唱歌 chàng gē (sing), 跳舞 tiào wǔ (dance), 骑自行车 qí zìxíngchē (ride a bike).
Activity: "Find someone who…": ask classmates 你会滑冰吗? and record names, then report: Lily 会滑冰, 但是不会滑雪。
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.

body.objective: Students will be able to interview a classmate about hobbies.

body.hook: Time to become a reporter. You'll interview a classmate about their hobbies and skills in Mandarin, then write a short profile, just like a student newspaper.

vocabulary.term: 多长时间 duō cháng shíjiān

study.title: 采访同学
study.question: How do I interview a classmate about hobbies in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Interview questions (written for this lesson):
1. 你的爱好是什么? Nǐ de àihào shì shénme? (What's your hobby?)
2. 你为什么喜欢…? (Why do you like…?)
3. 你常常跟谁一起…? (Who do you often do it with?)
4. 你学了多长时间? (How long have you learned it?)
5. 你会…吗? 你还会什么? (Can you…? What else can you do?)
Sample answers: 我的爱好是打篮球。因为打篮球很有意思, 所以我常常打。我常常跟朋友一起打。我学了三年。我还会游泳。
Grammar: 因为…所以… (because… so…). Frequency words go before the verb: 我常常打篮球。我有时候画画。
Profile model: 我的同学叫 Leo。他的爱好是滑冰。因为他觉得滑冰很好玩, 所以他每个周末都去滑冰。他常常跟哥哥一起去。他学了五年。他还会弹吉他。
Activity: interview a partner (record notes in pinyin or characters), then write a 6–8 sentence profile and share it.
study.source: Original interview and profile written for this lesson.
discussion: How long have they done it?
